title: Your account and permissions
lede: What OME sets on your account and why. Useful when something you expected to see is not there.

blocks.text: Your access is configured under **Main Access Rights** when OME creates the account. In the Legacy portal, most areas offer **full** or **restricted**, where restricted can be scoped to particular folders rather than the whole institution. The table below is the standard configuration for a new pre-clerkship course director.

blocks.caption: Standard Main Access Rights for a new course director
rows: Gives portal access without the ability to create other users.
Full, or scoped to your folders
You need to write and edit items. Folder scoping is used where a course should only touch its own bank.
Full, or scoped to your folders
You need to build and edit assessments for your course.
Deliberate. The category tree is shared across all historical data — you apply tags, you do not restructure the tree.
Not used by most pre-clerkship courses.
You need reporting to review performance and run item analysis.
This is what makes single sign-on resolve to your account.

blocks.title: Grading stays unchecked
blocks.text: Checking the Grading right turns the account into a **grader-only** account, which is not what a course director needs and will remove access you expect to have. If you have been given a grader account by mistake, the symptom is that you can see grading queues but not the question bank or assessment builder.

blocks.title: Why Categories is restricted
blocks.text: Roughly nine years of item data is tagged against the shared category tree. Renaming or moving a node silently changes what past reports mean. If your course needs a category that does not exist, ask OME to add it rather than working around the restriction.
If the External ID does not match what UH SSO sends, sign-in fails with the account-not-found error described in [Account and sign-in](#account). That is the single most common access problem.
